summary: California's Cape Horn: a Chumash sacred headland where a lighthouse, first lit in 1856, was rebuilt lower on the bluff in 1882.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: USLHS dates the station's establishment to 1855 and records keeper Parkinson from 1854; the lens arrived September 1855 and the light was lit 1 February 1856 (LighthouseFriends; nomination cites postponement to that date). The record's 1855 first_lit is the establishment year.
Two towers: the first (1854, rebuilt wider 1855) on the high bluff, and the present tower lit 20 June 1882; the nomination dates the present building 1881, USLHS 1882.

notes_for_editor: Thin on primary sources: 1850s-1880s Light-House Board reports are not in the corpus, so the building story rests on the NRHP nomination (a 1977 narrative without footnotes) and LighthouseFriends, whose Bache and Parkinson quotations are cited as quoted there. Sources disagree on Parkinson's tenure (USLHS 1854-1856; LighthouseFriends dismissed after ~6 months; nomination says he stayed to 1875), on the duplex date/steps (1905, 180 steps vs 1906, 280 steps) and dwelling (1911 vs 1912). Light-House Board 1896-97 volume holds two years' reports (entries 990 and 994); the 150-feet blasting is the earlier (fiscal 1896), 2,500 cubic yards the later; assignment by entry order. The 1895 fog signal modification appears in the fiscal-1895 report; the 518 hours figure is from the fiscal-1895 fog-signal table. Roster from USLHS only; no newspaper hits found for 1882. NRHP listing year (1981 in the record) not verified from a fetched NPS page, so omitted. The 'range_nm' in the record was not verified. Searches in the Chronicling America index returned nothing for 1882.
